paragraphs: Rav Nachman, son of Rav Gurya.

Shabbat 95a relates that he came to Nehardea. They asked him questions, and he could not answer properly; they told him, “Your teacher was a reed-cutter in the marsh.” Dikdukei Soferim reads Rav Chama bar Gurya.[^1][^2]

notes.text: The consulted Shabbat paragraph explicitly makes the questioners tell Gurya’s son, “Your teacher was a reed-cutter.” The direction of the speech is corrected accordingly.

Dikdukei Soferim is the contextual expansion of דק״ס. Hyman reports the alternative Rav Chama bar Gurya, whose patronymic lacks the father’s title found in the heading. The dialogue’s questioners are the speakers of “Your teacher.”
